title: needs-decision: the owner-marker journal has no repository target, and the anchor check can't pass for a fresh set's first issue
body:
<!-- idd-skill-authoring-publication: target=target-7821b11489769b6a; anchor=kurone-kito/idd-skill#2606; set=set-73863292d72b9ae7; session=claude-idd-fork-7331fc85bb5f; token=pub-f331d2733e2ca7db -->

## Background

Refs #2606, #2621 (non-blocking).

#2606/#2621 (merged 2026-09-05) gave `audit-authored-issue.mts` teeth
over the issue-authoring contract's owner-marker/publication-token
protocol. Authoring a fresh roadmap-and-children set for #2668 two days
later exercised that protocol for what looks like the first time since
the enforcement landed, and surfaced two related gaps in the protocol
itself — not in this repository's implementation of it.

**Sub-gap 1 — no repository designates a journal.** The protocol
(`docs/issue-authoring-skill.md` / `skills/issue-authoring/references/
contract.md`, "Authoring hold and release") requires every newly created
issue's publication-intent record to live on a `journal`: "for an
existing set, use the verified originating Stage 1 hold; for a
standalone set with no existing issue or anchor, use a pre-existing
repository-level authoring journal target designated by repository
policy... If neither location exists or its identity cannot be
verified, stop with `blocked-by-human` before creating any target."
Nothing designates such a target in this repository: `.github/idd/config.json`
has no `issueAuthoring` key at all, and `schemas/policy.schema.json` defines
no journal-shaped field anywhere in its schema (checked directly against
both files).

`#2668`'s four children (`#2669`-`#2672`) could use the roadmap itself
as journal once it existed ("for an existing set, use the verified
originating Stage 1 hold"), and this issue uses `#2606` as journal for
the same reason (see "This issue's own trail" below) — but a truly
standalone first issue, with no natural predecessor to piggyback on, has
nothing to use.

**Sub-gap 2 — the anchor-match check cannot pass for any self-anchored
first issue, journal or not.** This is the more fundamental gap:
designating a journal would not fix it. `checkAuthoringOwnerMarkerTrail`
(`src/scripts/audit-authored-issue.mts`, around the
`marker.anchor === publicationMarker.anchor` comparison) requires the
owner marker's `anchor` field to literally equal the publication
marker's `anchor` field. For any issue that becomes its own anchor (a
roadmap, or a standalone orphan/needs-decision issue with no parent),
the publication marker is written *before* the issue exists — so its
`anchor` field can only be an opaque placeholder, generated with no
knowledge of the issue's future number. The owner marker, posted
*after* creation, necessarily carries the real `owner/repo#number` once
the number is known. These two values can never be made equal by
construction, for any repository, journal or not.

**Evidence, from this repository's own current state:**

- `#2668`'s publication marker (first line of its body) reads
  `anchor=anchor-07fca840e7a868cf` — an opaque bootstrap token, minted
  before creation. Its owner marker (posted after creation) reads
  `anchor=kurone-kito/idd-skill#2668` — the real ref. Running
  `audit-authored-issue.mjs --shape roadmap --new-issue --comments-file
  <#2668's fetched comments>` against it, with no
  `--journal-comments-file` (sub-gap 1 leaves nothing to supply), exits
  with the usage error `--new-issue with --comments-file requires
  --journal-comments-file` rather than reaching the check at all; had a
  journal been available to supply, the check would still reach
  `hasQualifyingOwnerMarker` and fail there on the `marker.anchor !==
  publicationMarker.anchor` mismatch (sub-gap 2), since a journal alone
  does not resolve that comparison.
- `#2669`-`#2672` (children of `#2668`) *do* pass the full check
  genuinely, `--new-issue --comments-file --journal-comments-file`
  included, because by the time they were created `#2668` already
  existed with a real number, so their publication markers could name
  `anchor=kurone-kito/idd-skill#2668` directly — no opaque placeholder
  needed.
- `#2621` also passes fully in the historical record, for the same
  reason: `#2606` already existed as a real, closed issue before `#2621`
  was created, so `#2621`'s publication marker could name
  `anchor=kurone-kito/idd-skill#2606` directly.

The pattern is consistent: the check only passes when a **real,
pre-existing** issue is available to serve as anchor. It structurally
cannot pass for the first, self-anchored issue of any genuinely new
initiative — which is exactly the case a roadmap-authoring session hits
most often.

**This issue's own trail.** Publishing this issue hits the identical
problem this issue is about: it has no parent roadmap and no natural
predecessor issue of its own. Rather than repeat #2668's disclosed,
partially-degraded bootstrap (no journal, "not applicable" on that one
check), this issue instead acquired `#2606` — the issue that originated
this whole protocol — as its anchor: `#2606` was re-labeled
`status:authoring`, given a fresh `mode=acquire` owner marker for a new
set/session, and this issue's publication marker names
`anchor=kurone-kito/idd-skill#2606` directly (a real ref, known in
advance, exactly like `#2621`'s own trail). That makes this issue's own
`authoring-owner-marker-trail` check pass genuinely — but only because a
thematically-related closed issue happened to be available to reuse.
`#2606` picks up a transient `status:authoring` label for the duration
of this authoring hold (removed at release, same as any other target);
it is closed, so this has no functional effect on Discover or CI in the
meantime. A repository with no such convenient predecessor for a given
piece of work would still be stuck.

Not a duplicate: searched `journal bootstrap anchor`, `authoring journal
designated`, and `standalone set no existing issue` against the
open+closed tracker (no hits), and ran the reuse-first recent-window
scan (`gh issue list --state all --limit 20`) — no near-simultaneous
duplicate. `#2606` itself already anticipated needing a *complete
mechanical enforcement* of the marker trail (that is what it decided);
it did not anticipate this specific bootstrap case, which only becomes
observable once the enforcement it requested actually exists and gets
exercised against a fresh initiative.

## Proposed change

No single proposed change: this is a maintainer decision among the
options below, analogous to how #2606 itself was framed.

### Options for a maintainer to choose among

1. **Designate a repository-level journal via policy.** Add a new
   `issueAuthoring.*` config field (for example
   `issueAuthoring.authoringJournalIssue`, an `owner/repo#number` or a
   local issue number) that both the protocol prose and
   `audit-authored-issue.mts` can read as the pre-existing journal for
   a standalone set. This closes sub-gap 1 but not sub-gap 2: a
   self-anchored roadmap would still need to name its own
   not-yet-existent number in its publication marker's `anchor` field.
2. **Add a first-anchor bootstrap rule to the contract and the
   linter.** Recognize the case where a target's own `target` and
   `anchor` fields (owner marker) both equal the current issue's own
   identity, *and* its publication marker's `anchor` field is an
   opaque, never-otherwise-referenced token (i.e., this issue is
   genuinely its own anchor) — accept that shape as satisfying the
   anchor check, and exempt only this bootstrap case from the journal
   cross-check (an anchor cannot journal its own creation; downstream
   children of the same set still get the normal cross-check once the
   anchor is real). This closes sub-gap 2 directly and makes sub-gap 1
   irrelevant for the anchor's own creation specifically (children
   still benefit from option 1 if a repository also wants journal
   coverage for genuinely standalone non-roadmap issues).
3. **Formalize the "piggyback on a pre-existing related issue" pattern
   already used by #2621 and this issue.** Document it as the required
   authoring move whenever a new initiative has any plausible
   predecessor (a discussion issue, a decision issue, a prior
   roadmap), and accept that a truly first-of-its-kind initiative with
   no predecessor falls back to #2668's disclosed partial-degradation
   path (or is itself front-loaded as a `blocked-by-human` "create a
   journal issue first" step).
4. **Status quo — accept the gap.** The mechanical check stays
   skippable for this one case by omitting `--new-issue` (or supplying
   no `--journal-comments-file`), which is exactly the residual risk
   #2606 already flagged and #2621 only partially closed. A maintainer
   may judge this acceptable since the gap is narrow (only a fresh
   set's own anchor, not any of its children) and self-disclosing (the
   linter reports "not applicable" rather than a false pass).

None of these are mutually exclusive; a maintainer may pick more than
one (for example, 1 and 2 together give both a general journal and a
bootstrap exemption).

## Scope notes for whoever picks this up

- This is about `docs/issue-authoring-skill.md` (the canonical
  contract) and its generated mirrors
  (`skills/issue-authoring/references/*`,
  `.claude/skills/issue-authoring/`), and
  `src/scripts/audit-authored-issue.mts` /
  `src/scripts/marker-helpers.mts` if direction 1 or 2 is chosen.
- Do not relitigate #2606's own decision (mechanical enforcement was
  the right call) — this issue is scoped to the bootstrap case that
  enforcement's first real exercise (`#2668`) surfaced, not a reason to
  weaken enforcement generally.
